featured.name: Lisa
featured.tagline: A voice you can actually talk to.
featured.description: An AI-powered voice assistant combining speech recognition, language models, natural speech, and agentic web search.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Talking to software still means typing. Most voice interfaces stop at transcription — they can't hold a conversation, look something up, or answer in a voice that sounds human.

sections.title: The approach
sections.body: Built the full speech-to-speech loop: browser speech recognition feeds a FastAPI orchestration layer, which calls a language model with tool access for agentic web search, then streams synthesised speech back to the client. PostgreSQL keeps conversation memory between turns, and the React front end prioritises low-latency streaming over perfect-looking UI.

sections.title: The outcome
sections.body: A working assistant you can interrupt mid-sentence and keep talking to, deployed publicly on Vercel. It validated the architecture end to end: speech in, reasoning with tools, natural speech out.

featured.name: Spently
featured.description: A personal finance tracker for securely recording, categorizing, filtering, and visualizing everyday expenses.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Most budgeting tools are either a spreadsheet with extra steps or a black box that decides what your money means. Tracking a daily expense should take seconds, and the data should stay yours.

sections.title: The approach
sections.body: Django and PostgreSQL for authentication, records, and server-side filtering, with a category model that keeps reports consistent instead of relying on free-text tags. Chart.js renders the spend breakdown, and the query layer is written as reusable filters so new views don't duplicate business logic.

sections.title: The outcome
sections.body: A deployed app used for real day-to-day expense tracking, with a clean split between data and presentation and a filtering model that made every later view cheap to add.

featured.name: Maargam
featured.tagline: Directions that survive a dead signal.
featured.description: An offline-first public transport app designed to help commuters navigate Telangana bus services.

sections.title: The problem
sections.body: Bus commuters in Telangana rely on memory and word of mouth. The places where you most need route information — on the road, between towns — are exactly where connectivity is worst.

sections.title: The approach
sections.body: An offline-first Flutter architecture: route and timetable data ships with the app, is stored locally, and every search runs on-device. The interaction model favours fast lookups over dense maps, and the interface was sized for low-end Android phones in bright outdoor light.

sections.title: The outcome
sections.body: An app that works with aeroplane mode on, which was the whole point. It also laid the groundwork for live arrival data without changing the offline data model.
